extracted.intended_audience: students studying rhetoric/communication or readers analyzing commencement speeches
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing a comedic commencement speech with focus on rhetorical devices and persuasive strategies (ethos, pathos, repetition) and how humor is used to convey serious themes and engage an academic audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ethos
rubrics_metrics.description: O'Brien effectively uses ethos to establish his credibility and keep the audience engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: “Before I begin, I must point out that behind me sits a highly admired President of the United States and decorated war hero while I, a cable television talk show host, have been chosen to stand here and impart wisdom. I pray I never witness a more damning example of what is wrong with America today.” This self-deprecating joke both acknowledges his status and establishes credibility as a comedian, opening the speech with a joke to show the audience he knows what he is talking about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: O'Brien uses pathos to appeal to emotions and convey his primary points about change and growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay states Conan 'effectively uses ethos, pathos, and repetition to convey ... that change is inevitable and that how people are able to embrace change is what makes humans grow as a society.' Emotional appeals are used alongside humor to make the theme resonate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Repetition is used as a rhetorical device to reinforce the central message (that change is inevitable and embracing it leads to growth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repetition highlights and cements the speech's theme for the graduating audience; it functions alongside ethos and pathos to make the argument memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of literary devices generally
rubrics_metrics.description: The speech employs 'a plethora of literary devices' to help graduates better understand the primary points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond the named appeals, the analysis suggests multiple literary/rhetorical techniques are used throughout; effective speeches layer devices to clarify and emphasize themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy as persuasive strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: O'Brien uses comedy as a way to portray his thoughts and give a powerful speech about the trials and conflicts of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor is the vehicle for both critique and consolation—e.g., using a joke about being chosen over the President to criticize choices while establishing tone. Comedy allows treatment of serious topics in an accessible way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: keep it light and breezy / lighthearted and laid-back
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan's main focus was 'to keep it light and breezy to allow the audience to connect better' and to remain 'lighthearted and laid-back.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lighter tone makes complex or uncomfortable themes (change, trials, conflicts) approachable for graduates; maintaining this tone aids connection and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement and connection
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques that keep the audience engaged and allow them to connect with the speaker are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishing credibility, using humor, maintaining an accessible tone, and employing literary devices are all directed at keeping the audience engaged and giving them 'the chance to connect and stay.' Effective speeches prioritize audience rapport.
